https://nineoclock.ro/romanian-pm-ilie-b.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Meeting between Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan and European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan received today, at Victoria Palace, the European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib. The discussions focused on cooperation between Romania and the European Commission in the field of crisis management, strengthening preparedness and response capacity, enhancing European resilience, as well as promoting equal opportunities, inclusion and social resilience. An important topic of the meeting was Romania’s role in the European civil protection mechanisms, in the current security context. European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib thanked Romania for its constant contribution to joint efforts through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM), including by mobilizing teams and capabilities to fight wildfires in France, Greece and Serbia, as well as for the support granted in other emergency situations, including in the Gaza Strip. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan pointed out that Romania remains a stable and active partner in efforts to strengthen European emergency response capacity. “Romania has an integrated and centralized intervention system, with specialized structures and the capacity to rapidly mobilize the necessary forces. Romania has also benefited from significant equipment financed through European funds, and this support has contributed to strengthening our intervention capacity. We thank the EU for this support, which helps us be better prepared for emergency situations,” stated the Head of the Executive. The meeting also addressed the regional security context and the risks facing Romania, including incidents involving drones in the Black Sea area and in the vicinity of the Eastern Flank. In this context, Prime Minister Bolojan underlined the need to pay particular attention to the Black Sea region, calling for the support of the European Commission for the implementation of the Black Sea Resilience Platform, proposed by Romania as part of the European Union’s new strategic approach to the region. The initiative aims to strengthen regional cooperation and preparedness and response capacity in dealing with crisis situations and new types of risks. European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib welcomed Romania’s initiative regarding the Black Sea Resilience Platform and emphasized the importance, in the current context, of a forward-looking approach to risks, mentioning that a risk assessment will be published in November. The European Commissioner also stressed the need to improve communication and coordination among Member States in crisis situations, as well as to strengthen the role of the European Commission’s Emergency Response Coordination Centre in ensuring a rapid and coordinated response. “Romania is also an example regarding civil-military cooperation. Its experience can be a source of inspiration and a useful model for the development of these capabilities at European level,” stated European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib. Another topic of discussions was equal opportunities, combating discrimination and measures to promote social inclusion. The discussions covered measures aimed at increasing women’s participation in the labour market, particularly women from rural areas. The situation of the Roma community was also addressed, with emphasis placed on the need for effective public policies to combat discrimination, reduce social disparities and ensure equal access to education, employment and public services. Also attending the meeting, on behalf of the Government, were Secretary of State within the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Head of the Department for Emergency Situations (DSU), Dr Raed Arafat, and State Advisor at the Prime Minister’s Chancellery, Luminița Odobescu . https://www.deccanchronicle.com/world/pu.text: Slovakia: A teacher was fatally stabbed by a pupil at an elementary school in northwestern Slovakia on Tuesday during an attack in which two other people were seriously injured, authorities said.Police said a 13-year-old suspect was in police custody and that the situation was under control and there was no further threat to the public. A motive was not immediately known.The stabbings took place in Staškov, a small town near the border with the Czech Republic and Poland that has a population of some 2,750 people.The killed teacher was a 61-year-old woman. The injured included a pupil who was in critical condition and a 41-year-old female teacher who was hospitalized with serious injuries, Slovakis's rescue service said.President Peter Pellegrini said he was "deeply saddened by the tragic incident" at the school in Staskov. He and Prime Minister Robert Fico offered condolences to the victims' families."Such events serve as a serious warning to our entire society," Pellegrini said. "It is all the more important that we pay close attention to the atmosphere we create in society. We need more calm, respect, and mutual regard."Interior Minister Matúš Šutaj Eštok, Education Minister Tomáš Drucker and Health Minister Kamil Šaško traveled to the town.In 2025, an 18-year-old student fatally stabbed a 51-year-old deputy principal and an 18-year-old student at a high school in northern Slovakia.In 2020, a 22-year-old former student attacked a high school in the town of Vrutky, killing the deputy principal and wounding five people, including two students. In 2022, a high school student attacked and injured a female pupil at a high school in Novaky.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqx2.text: Image source, Lochrenberg family Image caption, Janine Lochrenberg had "a deep affinity with the water" her sister told the BBC By Ed Habershon Reporting from Johannesburg Published 17 minutes ago A South African woman has been killed in a shark attack off the country's east coast, in what is the first recorded such fatality this year. Janine Lochrenberg was swimming off a beach in KuGompo City (formerly East London) on Tuesday morning when she was attacked. Witnesses said the 65-year-old was bitten in two places and died before she was brought to shore. Shark attacks are rare in South Africa, with fewer than 10 fatal ones since 2012, according to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File. Lochrenberg was out on a daily morning swim with her local open water swimming club when she was attacked at around 08:00 (06:00 GMT). Fellow swimmers brought her to shore, but it's believed she died before they could get her out of the water. She was bitten on her thigh and her upper arm, one of her fellow swimmers told the BBC. They also said she had been wearing a magnetic shark repellent band on her ankle at the time. Lochrenberg's sister Margot said she was holding her sister's head as they brought her to shore but believed she bled out in the water. She told the BBC that her sister had "loved the water so much" despite knowing there was an "elevated shark presence in East London". "She'd made peace with that. She had a deep affinity with the water and was a remarkable person," she said. Barbara Briceland, Lochrenberg's partner, told the BBC the retired medical physicist was a good swimmer, who often swam far out into the breakers, and described her as very brave. "She was highly intelligent, lots of fun, kind, in a quietish way, thoughtful, well-loved with a love of life." Briceland added they were looking forward to retirement and were about to leave for a three-week road trip together. Orient Beach, where the attack took place, has been closed alongside another nearby beach, authorities confirmed.
